title: Emergence of modern human behaviour
summary: Abstract images in the Eurasian Upper Paleolithic, after about 35,000 years ago, were long taken as a sign of the cognition behind modern human behaviour. Engravings on red ochre at Blombos Cave in South Africa, dated to about 77,000 years ago, showed that these abilities are far older. Research at Middle Stone Age sites from 120,000 to 50,000 years ago now traces how they developed.

uncertainty.note: Start reflects the onset of Middle Stone Age symbolic and technological innovations across southern Africa (c. 120–100 ka); end corresponds to the widespread adoption of modern behaviors prior to global dispersals (c. 50 ka). Years converted from BP (1950 - cal BP).

where.historical_name: Southern coast of Africa, Middle Stone Age; no polities existed

importance.justification: The emergence of symbolic expression, abstract communication, and composite tool industries transformed human cognition, enabling Homo sapiens to adapt, coordinate, and outcompete or absorb other hominin populations across the globe.

related.because: The anatomical emergence of Homo sapiens in Africa provided the biological brain structure that enabled later symbolic and cultural modernization.
Complex symbolic communication and flexible composite technologies developed in the Middle Stone Age equipped modern humans to migrate and adapt across Eurasia.
The technological, symbolic, and social advantages developed during behavioural modernization allowed Homo sapiens to outcompete and absorb Neanderthal populations.
